Think of it as wallpaper trim, not a picture frame.

Step 1: Create the vertical strip asset (design logic)

You (or your image editor / generator) should extract or recreate one side only.

Target image specs (ideal)

  • Orientation: Vertical

  • Width: 120–240px (wide enough to read the art, narrow enough for UI)

  • Height: 800–1600px (taller = smoother repetition)

  • Background: Transparent PNG (best) or solid background matching site

Step 2: Use CSS to make it infinite (this is the magic)

HTML (minimal)

html

  <div class="content">

CSS (this does the infinite stacking)

css
.page {
  display: flex;
}

.content {
  flex: 1;
  padding: 40px;
}

/* shared border styles */
.paw-border {
  width: 160px; /* adjust to taste */
  background-image: url("/images/paw-border-vertical.png");
  background-repeat: repeat-y;
  background-position: center top;
  background-size: contain;
}

/* optional mirroring so you only need ONE image */
.paw-border.right {
  transform: scaleX(-1);
}

What’s happening here, scientifically speaking:

  • repeat-y tiles the image only vertically

  • The browser stacks copies endlessly as the page grows

  • No JavaScript required

  • Zero performance penalty

This is how professional sites do decorative rails.

Step 3: Mobile & responsiveness (don’t skip this)

css
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .paw-border {
    width: 80px;
    opacity: 0.5; /* optional elegance */
  }
}

You want it present but not overwhelming on small screens.

Step 4: Pro tip (makes it feel premium)

If the paws feel too rigid when repeated, you can:

  • Slightly fade the top & bottom edges of the image

  • Or add subtle vertical noise/grain
    This hides repetition artifacts from the human pattern-recognition machine (the brain).

The Core Principle (this is the key)

👉 Photos stay rectangular underneath

Universal HTML Structure (works for ALL your frames)

Base CSS (frame-ready, responsive, clean)

css
.frame{
  position: relative;
  width: 320px;
  aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
  overflow: hidden;
}

/* the photo */
.frame img:first-child{
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;       /* THIS is the magic */
  object-position: center; /* keeps faces centered */
}

/* frame overlay */
.frame-overlay{
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.frame.heart img:first-child{

  mask-repeat: no-repeat;
